email.subject: Delegated engineering at Capital One scale
email.body:
Hi James,

Your team's posts on delegating engineering work to agents stood out: an internal platform for monorepo migrations, then a Cursor pipeline that moved 180 Micronaut services. With Capital One committed to investing materially in Brex, the open question is who keeps maintaining that harness as the scope grows.

Devin is built for that work. It plans, codes and tests on its own VMs, splits big tasks across parallel cloud agents, and can deploy in your VPC, so your engineers act as architects and review the output. Teams at Ramp use Devin to fix tens of thousands of hours of technical debt.

Open to a short call on what your platform team would rather not own?

Best,

drafts.linkedin_note: James, I read Brex's posts on delegating engineering work to agents, from the gRPC migrations to the Micronaut 4 pipeline. I work on Devin at Cognition, which runs that kind of work across parallel cloud agents. Would be glad to connect and trade notes.

Both are workloads Devin takes as delegated tasks, with a human reviewing every PR before it merges. If it would help, I can share how Nubank scoped and sequenced theirs.

Hi Phil,

The Micronaut 4 write-up from your org was candid: local agent runs broke whenever a laptop slept, so the team provisioned self-hosted nodes, headless auth and a library of eleven skills before the pipeline held. It also says the remainder of the migration still needs de-risking, and that some services had gaps in their test suites.

Devin runs that loop as a product: it tests end to end on its own VMs, keeps working when the laptop is closed, and splits big tasks across parallel cloud agents. Nubank used Devin on migrations and reports an 8x engineering time efficiency gain.

Open to a short call on which parts of that harness your platform team could hand off?

Best,
